meta.title: Kajal Jotwani — software developer & creative coder
meta.description: Backend & systems developer who also makes art and music with code. GSoC '25 · C4GT '25 · open source. This site is an instrument — press play.

hero.roleLine: I build backends, break systems (on purpose), and sometimes make code sing.
hero.paragraph: Third-year CS undergrad into backend engineering, systems, and how intelligent things work under the hood. On the side, I turn algorithms into art and keystrokes into music.
hero.marginNote: this page is an instrument — try the ♪ up there

paragraphs: I'm a third-year Computer Science undergrad who likes the unglamorous parts of software: the backends, the protocols, the systems that quietly hold everything up. Currently diving into AI and MCP — understanding how modern intelligent systems are actually built genuinely fascinates me.

I contribute to open source because it's the best classroom I've found. And when I'm not shipping, I'm usually making generative art or live-coding music — the same loops and functions, just pointed at beauty instead of throughput.
funFacts: if I'm not coding, I'm probably running or at the gym
fueled by coffee, curiosity, and dreams bigger than my comfort zone

experience.intro: step by step, curiosity did the steering — tap a step for the full story.

entries.title: Google Summer of Code — Contributor
entries.short: Built VR experiences for an open-source XR project.
entries.detail: Selected as a GSoC '25 contributor with the UC Open Source Program Office. Worked on Brahma-XR, exploring VR development end to end — Three.js scenes, Blender asset pipelines, and custom shaders. Learned how real open-source teams review, argue, and ship.

entries.title: Code for GovTech — Contributor
entries.short: Built an Education Management Information System used by a district administration.
entries.detail: As a C4GT '25 contributor, built an EMIS for the Additional Deputy Commissioner's office in Karnal — real users, real data, real constraints. Learned what 'production' means when the stakeholder is a government office and downtime is not a vibe.

entries.title: LiFT Scholar
entries.detail: Awarded a Linux Foundation Training (LiFT) scholarship — doubling down on systems, Linux, and the infrastructure side of software.

entries.title: Women Engineers Scholar
entries.short: Selected for the WE program by Google and TalentSprint.
entries.detail: Chosen as a Women Engineers scholar '24 — a two-year engineering excellence program by Google and TalentSprint with mentorship, rigorous coursework, and a community of women who build.

projects.intro: turn ♪ on, then hover a waveform — every project has its own beat.

items.name: Brahma-XR
items.description: An open-source XR project under the UC Open Source Program Office, where immersive experiences are built with web technologies.
items.myWork: Built and refined VR scenes with Three.js and WebXR; created and optimized 3D assets in Blender; wrote custom shaders for visual effects; collaborated through the full open-source workflow — issues, reviews, iterations — as a Google Summer of Code 2025 contributor.

items.name: EMIS for ADC Karnal
items.oneLiner: An Education Management Information System for a district administration.
items.description: A GovTech system built under Code for GovTech 2025 to help the ADC office in Karnal manage education data across the district.
items.myWork: Designed and built core modules of the EMIS — data models, backend logic, and workflows shaped by conversations with actual government stakeholders. Shipped something a public office depends on, which changed how I think about reliability and simplicity.

items.name: This website
items.oneLiner: A portfolio disguised as an instrument.
items.description: The page you're on. A professional portfolio with a secret: the scroll bar is a playhead, the background is a score, and the keyboard makes music when you let it.
items.myWork: Designed and built with Next.js and a hand-rolled WebAudio engine — no audio libraries. The background is a generative flow field, keystrokes play an FM e-piano, and every project card gets a drum groove seeded by its own name. All copy lives in one JSON file, and the score is live-codeable at /play.
